Verb rendered by the phrasal led ... astray, discontinuous around the object (rule 25). astray is a directional particle that names nothing on its own, as away and forth do in rule 44's put away and take away, so the head stays on the lexical verb. Heading on astray was the competing reading, and it is what this chapter's other phrasal verbs (compassed about, carried away, fell out) would have had to be changed to.

review_notes: The margin's compelled Judah thereto was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).

led ... astray heads on led. astray is a phrasal particle of the kind rule 44 keeps with its verb, naming nothing on its own exactly as away does in put away and take away, so the head stays on the lexical verb as it does for the chapter's other phrasal verbs at 21.9 (compassed about), 21.17 (carried away) and 21.19 (fell out). astray was the competing head; the chapter reconciliation pass moved it there from astray to led.
The causative made ... to play the harlot is a different construction and is untouched: it is rule 44's light verb with a lexical complement, headed on play.
